node-1.label: New pigmented lesion on left second toenail, progressively growing for 12 months

node-2.label: Male in his 40s, first presentation for this problem, no prior treatments attempted, lesion asymptomatic

node-3.label: Physical examination showed dark brown longitudinal pigment band covering full length of left second toenail with nail thickening, pigment same width throughout and extending to proximal nail fold

node-4.label: No other nail or skin lesions found on examination; patient otherwise well with no fevers or weight loss

why.why: Histopathology, the gold standard, refutes malignant melanocytic nail tumor: no melanocytic proliferation, negative S100/CD34, bland spindle cell proliferation with epithelial invaginations and fibroepithelial projections into the nail plate, plus intracorneal hemorrhage and hyperkeratosis. Both expert analyses conclude this is a benign fibroepithelial/matricial process rather than melanoma, and the proximal nail fold extension is best explained as a hemorrhage-related pseudo-Hutchinson sign. Therefore confidence in malignant nail tumor is reduced from 0.75 to 0.05.

Histopathology reveals no melanocytic proliferation, negative S100/CD34, bland spindle cell proliferation with epithelial invaginations, and hemorrhage/hyperkeratosis. Expert analyses favor a benign onychopapilloma or reactive fibroepithelial/matricial process. The previously concerning proximal nail fold extension is explained as pseudo-Hutchinson sign from hemorrhage, removing the main atypical feature. Confidence in benign pigmented nail lesion is increased to 0.85.

Histopathology provides no evidence of infection and instead demonstrates bland spindle cell proliferation, epithelial invaginations, hemorrhage, and hyperkeratosis, favoring a benign fibroepithelial/matricial process. The pigment band pattern and proximal nail fold involvement are atypical for onychomycosis. Therefore confidence in nail infection/onychomycosis is lowered to 0.05.
